note: Single source of truth for what each cue-vox mode can do. Both layers read this file: the TECHNICAL layer (what tools/blocks fire) and the BEHAVIORAL layer (the prompt that tells the agent its ceiling). Edit here; nothing else hardcodes these rules.

dispositions.full: Render the widget / fire the tool normally, shown on screen.
dispositions.deflect: Do not render. Recognize the request, beat, offer a voice-doable alternative as a yes/no, then branch.
dispositions.run_unshown: The tool runs underneath (rails stay wired), but no widget is surfaced.

narrowing_shades: The input shades are how the system converges a conversation toward executable steps. Y/N is the binary shade (available in every mode). Scalar (a dial/degree) and generic text (open capture) are finer shades, available only on the full Baseline surface. In the ceiling modes (Expressive, Live) the only shade you can surface is Y/N. Scalar and text both ride the INPUT tag, so at the technical layer they move together.

deflection.offer_template: From here, want to move forward with {alt}?
deflection.future: When the yes/no loop is solid, the offer can grow a 'hold it?' tail that parks the request and resurfaces it when a mode can carry it. Rides the same loop; no rework.

surface_policy.yes_no: Be eager to narrow the conversation toward an executable step, and the yes/no is how you do it here: when things reach a real fork or a step you could actually take, put it as a yes/no and drive forward. Every yes/no must move one step closer to doing something. The one thing to never do is render a yes/no that narrows nothing: never to acknowledge, to fill a turn, to check in, or because a yes/no was mentioned, and never a yes/no about whether to show a yes/no. Converge, do not stall, and do not spin.

brevity_stance.note: Baseline only. The brevity dial (scalar 0..1, where 0 = max brevity / deliverable / tight and 1 = reflective / loose) sets how hard the agent narrows toward executable steps. Bands are ordered ascending by max_b; the first band whose max_b is >= the dial value applies.

bands.stance: Brevity is maxed. Treat the current model as correct and stable. Do not propose or make changes on your own. Before changing ANYTHING in our model, stop and ask first: 'are you sure you want to change anything in our model?' Add zero new surface.
Brevity is high. Narrow hard: drive every loose end toward an executable step. Prefer a tight yes/no or a scalar over open discussion. Close threads, do not open new ones.
Medium brevity. Converge when a real fork appears and put the decision plainly, but leave room to explore around it.
Low brevity. Explore: expand options, think out loud, do not force convergence.

roadmap.input: form is the NEXT capability, built as a standalone modular TOOL (not baked into cue-vox). cue-vox is its first caller; the browser plugin becomes a second caller of the same contract. Until it ships, input deflects.
